item.title: Park rangers and residents speak up to save Togo's last national park
item.description: A few years ago, I drove with an old friend from Togo, West Africa, towards the country's last remaining large protected area, Fazao-Malfakassa National Park. Our destination was the Hotel Fazao, where his uncle had once worked as a professional chef after its opening in 1980. For decades, while the park was managed by the Swiss Franz Weber Foundation (FWF), the hotel had hosted tourists from around the world who came to see elephants, monkeys, and other wildlife for which Africa is famous. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI governance model inspired by Pope Leo XIV aims to put ethics first
item.description: Researchers at the John Paul II Catholic University of Lublin (KUL) and the University of Eastern Finland have developed a new model of artificial intelligence governance inspired by the teachings of Pope Leo XIV as set out in his encyclical Magnifica Humanitas. The new model is intended to ensure that AI technologies are developed and used safely, fairly and with full respect for human rights. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Bumpy battery surfaces can masquerade as nanoscale ion pathways, misleading material design
item.description: A signal that appears to show ions moving inside a battery may, in fact, be an illusion caused by an uneven surface. A KAIST research team has identified the origin of this type of artifact, which can lead researchers to misinterpret what is happening inside a battery, and has developed a method to reduce it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Survey of young researchers raises concerns over future of science in U.S.
item.description: One-third of young scientists who had been planning careers in academic research changed their minds in the spring of 2025, according to a new survey. Fewer expected to remain in higher education or work in the U.S., or felt that pursuing a Ph.D. was the right decision. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: From strays to territory bosses: Epigenetics makes cheetahs adaptable
item.description: The findings of a new study led by the Leibniz-IZW on Namibian free-ranging cheetahs (Acinonyx jubatus jubatus) demonstrate that epigenetic mechanisms might play an important role in how animals develop different phenotypes despite their low genetic diversity. The work is published in the journal Molecular Ecology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A child's first 5 years set them up for life. African study explores how to target education spending
item.description: The first five years of life lay an important foundation for children's future schooling, health and earnings. Yet over 77% of children in sub-Saharan Africa don't have access to early childhood care and education. This places them at risk of not reaching their development potential. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Deep biosphere has endured mountain-building and erosion over hundreds of millions of years
item.description: A new study reveals that microbial life deep within Earth has persisted and repeatedly flourished through hundreds of millions of years of mountain-building and erosion. By analyzing minerals, fluids and gases from a 2.3-kilometer-deep (1.4-mile-deep) borehole in central Sweden, researchers have uncovered episodic bursts of methane-producing life linked to major geological events that shaped Scandinavia. The paper is published in the journal Communications Earth & Environment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The listening gap is real—how AI might help teachers bridge it
item.description: A Grade 4 teacher showed her class a video of children who walk miles barefoot to school. A hand shot up: "Why are you showing us AI slop? No way this is real." Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists tagged 14,000 endangered moths with paint and glue; none turned up, and that may be good news
item.description: In a groundbreaking study, researchers have tagged over 14,000 Bogong moths in the Snowy Mountains of Australia. However, after extensive tracking efforts, none have been recaptured, suggesting potential populations larger than previously assumed. Alternatively, these moths might be utilizing undiscovered migration routes. The ongoing project remains crucial for understanding the ecology of these endangered insects. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: 'The Jungle Book' offers an unconventional tool for undergraduate economics education
item.description: Research in the International Journal of Pluralism and Economics Education argues that "The Jungle Book" can serve as an unconventional teaching tool for undergraduate economics, using the original stories by Rudyard Kipling as well as Disney film adaptations to introduce concepts ranging from scarcity and sustainability to happiness and development. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Weak hydrogen bonds dethrone copper as the most stable metal binder, opening a new path for metal selection
item.description: Copper has been knocked off the top of a stability ranking it had dominated for decades. Without altering the atoms directly bonded to the metal, a KAIST research team reversed the longstanding trend in which copper generally forms the most stable complexes by tuning only the weak hydrogen bonds in its surrounding environment. The findings, which appear in the Journal of the American Chemical Society, could open new avenues for selective metal separation and recognition, as well as catalyst design. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Inexpensive blue pigment enables efficient one-step conversion of carbon dioxide to methane
item.description: A common blue pigment could help turn carbon dioxide (CO₂) from an industrial waste product into a useful fuel. A joint research team led by Tohoku University's Advanced Institute for Materials Research (WPI-AIMR), in collaboration with Hokkaido University and startup AZUL Energy, has developed a catalyst that converts CO₂ directly into methane (CH₄) with high efficiency using copper phthalocyanine, an inexpensive and readily available blue pigment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ships, ice cores and krill surveys underpin Australia's 10-year Antarctic monitoring strategy
item.description: The important role ships play in gathering scientific data in Antarctica and the Southern Ocean has been outlined at a leading Antarctic science conference in Hobart. The biennial Australian Antarctic Research Conference was held at the University of Tasmania and attracted 400 researchers from around the globe. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why 'you're smart' can backfire: Young children may cheat more after ability praise
item.description: Parents and teachers might think telling kids "they're smart" is a helpful way to build self-confidence and support positive development. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Stripped-down LSD reveals structural features linked to hallucinogenic and therapeutic effects
item.description: University of California, Davis, researchers have stripped down LSD to the base features responsible for its hallucinogenic and therapeutic effects. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New nitride semiconductor expands material options for more powerful electronics
item.description: Polar wurtzite nitride semiconductors, such as aluminum nitride (AlN) and gallium nitride (GaN), are central to modern high-power and high-frequency electronic devices because of their wide band gaps, high breakdown electric fields, and strong spontaneous and piezoelectric polarization. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Heel-strike' may have allowed early humans to walk farther—at the cost of high-impact forces
item.description: The average person takes thousands of steps each day, instinctively walking heel-to-toe. Although they hardly register them, those consistent heel-first strides are more distinctive to humans than previously thought and allowed early hominins to walk farther and more efficiently, but at the cost of higher impact forces on bones and joints, according to a new study led by a researcher at Penn State. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Slender crystal's blue-to-yellow glow could make invisible forces visible
item.description: Applying pressure to luminescent organic crystals usually brings molecules closer together and weakens their fluorescence. Materials that instead brighten and undergo a large color change are rare, and clear design principles for achieving both responses in simple, rigid aromatic hydrocarbons have been lacking. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What can a pair of underpants tell you about your vegetable garden?
item.description: This summer, 115 participants in Leiden and The Hague worked with scientists from Leiden University to investigate the soil life in their community garden plots. With mangetout peas, a taste test, a buried pair of underpants and a harvest festival, they helped scientists better understand the connection between soil, plants and people. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Neutrophil vesicles help Candida albicans evade immune-cell engulfment
item.description: The immune system is a highly sophisticated defense network designed to protect against pathogens. A research team from the Universities of Würzburg and Jena and the Leibniz Institute for Natural Product Research and Infection Biology (Leibniz-HKI) has shown that certain components of the immune system can actually help the yeast Candida albicans evade immune attack. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Yes, passing 1.5 C of global warming is cause for alarm, but not despair
item.description: The news has been full of headlines about findings from a United Nations report: The world is set to exceed the 1.5°C global warming target set out in the 2015 Paris Agreement. The report has raised concerns and questions about what a 1.5°C increase could mean for our world. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Reversible electric control unlocks persistent chiral phonon states
item.description: Atoms in a material are rarely still. They jiggle back and forth in collective lattice vibrations known as phonons. Their motion can also carry a rotational element: In 2023, scientists at PSI experimentally proved the existence of chiral phonons, which exhibit handedness depending on which way they rotate. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New report offers lessons for preserving cultural heritage in crisis zones
item.description: The report, "Digital heritage preservation for vulnerable collections: Reflections on the Sudan Memory project history and inventory," was authored by Dr. Laura Gibson, senior lecturer in digital content management education at King's, alongside Sara El-Nager, independent researcher and editor, and Dr. Hannah Ishmael, lecturer in digital culture & race. It draws on 14 interviews conducted by El-Nager with contributors to the Sudan Memory project, the first mass digitization project ever undertaken in Sudan. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Entangled particles revive a 35-year-old test of the Standard Model
item.description: Physicists at the BESIII Collaboration have breathed new life into a decades-old test of one of the Standard Model's most important ideas, using a technique that had gone almost untouched by experimenters for 35 years. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Organic farming outperforms wildflower strips on profits while both improve farm biodiversity
item.description: What makes more sense when farming wheat—strips of wildflowers along fields or organic farming? Both options provide financial support via the European Union as environmentally friendly and sustainable farming practices. An international research team, including researchers from the University of Göttingen, has compared the ecological and economic benefits of these two farming methods in fields planted with winter wheat. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Can atmospheric methane removal limit peak warming?
item.description: In a new report, the United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) concludes that global warming is expected to exceed 1.5°C within the next few years. This makes two questions increasingly important: how high will temperatures rise, and how long will the increase last? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Self-processing brain systems show both conservation and reorganization across primates
item.description: New in JNeurosci, Ning Liu, from the Institute of Biophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, explored whether brain structures for self-processing are conserved across primates, including humans, chimpanzees and macaques. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Excavations at Prado Vargas now span 140 square meters of a Neanderthal layer
item.description: The 2026 field season at Prado Vargas Cave, located in the village of Cornejo in the northern province of Burgos, Spain, within the Ojo Guareña karst complex, has expanded the excavation of Neanderthal sublevel 4D by 32 square meters (344 square feet), bringing the total excavated area to 140 square meters (1,507 square feet). More than 1,500 animal remains and stone tools were recovered, strengthening the interpretation of this roughly 46,000-year-old layer as a large Neanderthal camp. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Could bats self-medicate? More than 50 wild bats offer clues
item.description: When humans get sick, we change our routines and try various solutions to feel better and get well, like staying in bed to rest, going to the doctor, getting medication from the pharmacy, using home remedies and more. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Dark plasma regions reveal overlooked source of reactive atomic oxygen
item.description: Scientists from Tokyo Metropolitan University have found a way to make plasma more effective for its wide-ranging uses, from antimicrobial applications to surface conditioning in the semiconductor industry. They mapped the production of atomic oxygen, a key ingredient of oxygen plasma, while a high voltage was applied across oxygen gas. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Galileo, Copernicus, Cleansky, IRIS² must work together to secure Europe's place in the space race
item.description: "Seeing the Earth from above is a powerful reminder of our interdependence," said Thomas Pesquet. The words of France's 10th astronaut to head into space are a reminder of how we are "in this together," something the world's aerospace industry players should take heed of as they gather in Paris for the first International Space Summit from Sept. 9–10. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Fascinating read on how ancient societies handled natural hazards. So much we can still learn from how they built to adapt and recover, especially with climate extremes today. That view of the Roman Forum really puts it in perspective. Shakil Ahmed Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Tiny polymer particles keep water jets stable for longer
item.description: Tiny, soft polymer particles—known as microgels—can help to stabilize extremely thin liquid jets. How this works is the finding of a study led by researchers at TU Darmstadt, which has been published in Nature Communications. The findings could be of interest for the development of needle-free medical injection systems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The DESI legacy imaging survey releases the largest 2D map of the universe
item.description: In 2012, the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) was commissioned to measure the effect of dark energy, the mysterious force driving the expansion of the cosmos. Since then, the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys have obtained optical images of tens of millions of galaxies and quasars, including through NOIRLab's Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory (KPNO). In recent news, the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys team made its 11th data release (DR 11), constituting the largest-ever 2D map of the universe. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Pair of white dwarfs locked in 6-minute orbit might one day be observed by gravitational waves
item.description: Current gravitational-wave observatories aren't sensitive enough to capture the gravitational waves of binary stars. They can only see the gravitational chirps of black holes just as they are merging. But that will change as more sensitive instruments are developed. Recently, a team of astronomers discovered a binary white dwarf system that could be a good target for advanced gravitational-wave observatories. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New model measures economic risks solar storms pose to US power grid
item.description: In 1967, a solar storm nearly triggered World War III by jamming early-warning radar systems in the United States, causing U.S. leaders to think the Soviet Union was responsible. Though society averted catastrophe thanks to timely information from solar forecasters, the threat from space weather remains real. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A vital native bee highway can start in your own backyard
item.description: When it comes to bees, most of us can identify the ubiquitous honey bee (Apis mellifera) and that's about it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How 'hyperselection' is making modern life efficient, pleasant—and boring
item.description: It's difficult to imagine a song like Queen's 1975 "Bohemian Rhapsody" topping the charts today. Almost six minutes long, it moves through several radically different musical sections and famously ignores the conventional structure of a pop song. It seems almost designed to break the rules of what a hit single should be. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Two-color X-ray pulses capture the same nanoparticle at two moments in time
item.description: One big dream of ultrafast science has been to watch changes in nanoparticles or biomolecules on their natural timescale. Experimentally, this can be realized by taking two snapshots of the same object only femtoseconds apart. However, no detector is fast enough to record the two snapshots separately—they end up on top of each other in a single image. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: We teach students how to argue. But are we teaching them how to listen?
item.description: Picture a senior English classroom. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Reconstructed ancient protein maps how bacterial enzymes evolved distinct functions
item.description: How do related proteins develop different functions? This is the question investigated by a research team involving Kiel University, DESY and the Center for Structural Systems Biology (CSSB). Led by Holger Sondermann, professor at Kiel University and head of the Structural Microbiology group at DESY, the researchers reconstructed the common ancestor of two bacterial enzymes and produced the long-extinct protein in the laboratory. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New blending method gives common polymers a visible, reversible stress signal
item.description: Polymeric materials, such as plastics and rubbers, are essential in everyday life. However, detecting where mechanical stress is concentrated inside them remains a challenge. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What happens when you flush? Study reveals how toilet aerosols reach the breathing zone
item.description: Researchers from Flinders University have found that flushing toilets can release aerosols and bioaerosols into the surrounding air, with some studies detecting particles at heights corresponding to adults' breathing zones. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tragedia y dudas en Miami: los puntos oscuros detrás del accidente del avión de carga de Amazon
item.description: ¿Falla humana o viento en contra? La primeras hipótesis toman fuerza tras el accidente del Boeing 767. Investigadores analizan si la nave tocó la pista demasiado tarde. También examinarán el historial de mantenimiento de este avión que pasó por manos rusas. Fuente: Clarín - Mundo.

item.title: Isar Aerospace ha hecho historia con su cohete Spectrum. Europa occidental ya tiene acceso propio al espacio
item.description: La carrera espacial privada europea acaba de dar un gran paso adelante con el lanzamiento exitoso del cohete Spectrum desde el centro espacial de Andøya, en Noruega. La compañía alemana Isar Aerospace ya había hecho un intento en marzo de 2025. Sin embargo, terminó cayendo de nuevo a Tierra poco después de su lanzamiento. Ahora, se ha logrado llevar sin problemas a su destino, de modo que se ha convertido en el primer cohete puesto en órbita desde Europa Occidental. En el pasado , se lanzaron muchos cohetes desde el lado ruso, pero esta parte de Europa había necesitado siempre plataformas de… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Genomic analysis clarifies origin of unusual tail in endangered Tsushima leopard cat
item.description: Tsushima leopard cats are an endangered species found only on this isolated island. The most recent government survey estimated the population at around 150 individuals, and because domestic cats also inhabit the same landscape, introgression is a legitimate conservation concern. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Isle of Jura research casts new light on how rivers carve through landscapes
item.description: The waters of the remote Scottish island of Jura have long been famous for making whiskey. Now, the island's rivers have helped geologists learn more about how rivers erode rocks, providing new evidence that what streams carry plays an important role in how they carve through landscapes. Fuente: Phys.org.

Ver más Fascinating read on how ancient societies handled natural hazards. So much we can still learn from how they built to adapt and recover, especially with climate extremes today. That view of the Roman Forum really puts it… Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Rare pulsar unleashes 114 giant pulses in a single hour
item.description: Astronomers have detected extreme, never-before-seen behavior from a rare kind of pulsar and stumbled on a surprising link to one of astronomy's biggest current mysteries. Using 174 hours of radio observations, researchers detected PSR J1227-4853, a rapidly spinning neutron star known as a "transitional millisecond pulsar," which unleashes hundreds of ultrashort, ultrapowerful "giant pulses." Their paper was published in The Astrophysical Journal on July 31. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Investments promising social or environmental benefits need tougher anti‑greenwashing rules
item.description: Investment funds increasingly promise to deliver social or environmental benefits alongside financial returns. Regulators rightly ask whether these "impact investment" claims are accurate. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Dog parks are an antidote to the isolation and divisions that social media can fuel
item.description: The case against social media has become so well rehearsed that most people can easily merge it into ordinary conversation: It makes people lonely. It sorts them into camps. It hands them a room full of people who already agree with them and calls that a community. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Decades-old museum specimens reveal 10 extraordinary new worms
item.description: Scientists have discovered that one of the most unusual creatures in the animal kingdom is far more diverse and evolutionarily complex than previously known. An international team led by the University of Göttingen has reconstructed the evolutionary history of branching marine worms—rare annelids that live hidden inside sea sponges and whose bodies branch repeatedly into multiple posterior ends. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: China and Russia launch first sea ice survey aboard Xuelong 2 as Arctic tensions swell
item.description: China and Russia have conducted their first joint on-site sea ice survey in the Arctic Ocean aboard the Xuelong 2 research icebreaker, as tensions continue to rise over economic opportunities in the rapidly warming northern region. Two researchers from Russia’s Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute boarded Xuelong 2 as part of China’s 16th Arctic Ocean Expedition, according to a report by state broadcaster CCTV on Saturday. According to Lin Long, captain of the Xuelong 2 sea ice team, this... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Bela

item.title: Do black holes have hidden hair? Scientists find a new way to check
item.description: When two black holes crash together and merge, the newly formed black hole rings like a bell, sending out gravitational waves with specific frequencies that fade over time. This brief, fading pattern of waves is called ringdown, and it may hold secrets about what is hiding around black holes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Behind the scenes: The science that confirmed Australia's first H5 bird flu case
item.description: When a suspected case of H5 bird flu arrived in Australia, CSIRO scientists knew the first hours would matter. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Así serían los nuevos uniformes de la Fuerza Espacial de Estados Unidos. Alguien no entendió de qué iba 'Star Wars'
item.description: Cuando George Lucas ideó el universo 'Star Wars' , bebió de un montón de fuentes. Para su fantasía aventurera espacial se inspiró en Kurosawa y en el western, pero necesitaba una identidad para los 'malos'. El Imperio representaba la opresión y el control, siendo una representación absoluta del mal, y la asociación con el Tercer Reich estaba más que clara. Algo similar pasó cuando Paul Verhoeven ejecutó su adaptación libre de 'Starship Troopers', con los protagonistas a los que seguimos formando parte de una maquinaria totalitaria y extremista en una sátira antifascista . El diseño de algunos… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Alcolea

item.title: SpaceX rival launches rocket in historic first, says industry is 'desperate' for more
item.description: Isar Aerospace reached orbit on its second test flight as the German rocket startup looks to scale production amid booming satellite launch demand. Fuente: CNBC - World.

item.title: How researchers are helping Canada understand a changing climate
item.description: More than two dozen University of Victoria researchers contributed to "Canada's Changing Climate Report 2026," the country's most comprehensive assessment of how climate change is affecting communities, ecosystems and coastlines across Canada. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: White paper suggests 5 ways K–12 leaders can strengthen teacher recognition beyond appreciation weeks
item.description: University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies has published a new white paper, "Beyond Appreciation Weeks: Building Teacher Recognition Into the Everyday Work of K–12 Leadership," by Contessa Walker-Jackson, Ed.D., alumni fellow with the University's Center for Educational and Instructional Technology Research (CEITR). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: One quarter of Australian kids are 'developmentally vulnerable' when they start school
item.description: We know the first five years are a crucial time in a child's life. Early experiences, such as family relationships or exposure to trauma, shape brain architecture, which lays the foundation for children's learning, behavior and health. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists discovered an underwater city of 20,000 octopus nests deep inside California coast
item.description: In a remarkable finding, researchers have identified the largest nursery for octopuses off the Californian coast, aptly termed the 'Octopus Garden.' This incredible site is alive with thousands of pearl octopuses that mate and nest in the warm waters accelerated by nearby hydrothermal vents. Females diligently tend to their eggs until they hatch, giving life in their final moments as their bodies replenish the food chain for other deep-sea creatures. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Feeling angry? Don't blow off steam. Try these tips instead
item.description: After a bad night's sleep, you squabble with your kids at breakfast. Then a neighbor blocks you in. When you finally get to work an hour late, your boss makes one more impossible demand. No wonder you're angry with the world. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The 20th data release of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey
item.description: The Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), the largest multispectral imaging and spectroscopic redshift survey of the cosmos, has released its 20th data release (DR 20). It is also the third release of the survey's fifth phase (SDSS-V), representing a massive operational expansion of the legacy established with prior releases. This milestone provides an unprecedented look at the stars, the interstellar medium (ISM) and distant galaxies that make up the cosmos. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Three quantum phases in chromium-based material hint at a spin-triplet superconductor
item.description: Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity without electrical resistance when cooled below a specific critical temperature. These materials have proved promising for the development of various technologies, including medical imaging instruments, particle accelerators, ultrasensitive detectors and quantum processors. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Anna Conda ha comentado: Ornamental hermit
item.description: What's an old-fashioned job that no longer exists—like a lamplighter or a telegraph operator—that you think you'd be great at? Fuente: National Geographic.

item.description: What's an old-fashioned job that no longer exists—like a lamplighter or a telegraph operator—that you think you'd be great at? Ornamental hermit Ver más comentarios Anna Conda Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: German startup carries out Europe's first commercial space launch
item.description: German startup Isar Aerospace successfully launched its Spectrum rocket into orbit from Norway on Saturday night, marking the first ever such launch by a commercial entity from European soil. European firms are racing to make up ground in the lucrative launch industry, currently dominated by America's SpaceX. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: How Ancient Farmers Used Floral Designs to Track Goods
item.description: A Mesopotamian culture’s decorated ceramics show some early roots of math, researchers argued. Fuente: The New York Times - World.
item.dc:creator: Franz Lidz

item.title: Treat education as infrastructure during wartime, say researchers in Ukraine
item.description: War destroys laboratories and instruments. It also severs the human networks through which science reproduces itself. It disrupts mentorship, collaborations and informal ties that turn students into researchers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: BepiColombo begins Mercury arrival with MTM separation success
item.description: On 3 September 2026 at 15:49 CEST, the European Space Agency's BepiColombo Mission Control Team at the European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) received the signal they had been waiting for – BepiColombo’s Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) successfully separated from the spacecraft stack . This landmark achievement for the ESA and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) mission marks the first step of BepiColombo's long-awaited arrival at Mercury. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: 'Truly scared': Blazes outpace firefighters in Indonesian Borneo
item.description: Toiling around the clock, haggard Indonesian firefighters on the island of Borneo cannot keep up with the blazes devouring landscapes and shrouding communities in a cloying haze. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Can dogs sniff cancer? AI joins the hunt in India
item.description: When rescue dog Chloe is not tumbling across the grass on a farm outside India's tech capital, Bengaluru, she is learning to sniff human breath for cancer with a little help from AI. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Europe's space future in focus at the International Space Summit
item.description: The International Space Summit, taking place in Paris, France, on 9 and 10 September, will bring together world leaders, ministers, industry representatives and astronauts at a pivotal moment for the future of space. ESA Director General Josef Aschbacher will invite European leaders to reflect on the role Europe wishes to play in the next era of space exploration and on the level of ambition needed to help shape it. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: Advanced optical imaging reveals hidden activity in blood immune cells
item.description: A routine blood sample contains a diverse collection of immune cells that can reveal important clues about health and disease. These cells, known as peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), are widely used to study infections, autoimmune disorders, cancer and the immune system's response to treatment. Scientists typically identify these cells using fluorescent labels that attach to specific surface markers. While effective, those methods provide limited information about how the cells are functioning and can alter the cells during preparation. As reported in Biophotonics Discovery, a… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Popular brain supplement linked to shorter lifespan in men
item.description: A large study involving more than 270,000 people has linked higher blood levels of the amino acid tyrosine to a shorter lifespan in men. Using both observational data and genetic analysis, researchers found that elevated tyrosine could potentially reduce male life expectancy by nearly a year, while no significant effect appeared in women. Tyrosine is found naturally in protein-rich foods and is also sold as a supplement for boosting focus and mental performance, making the finding especially intriguing. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: How bird movements are helping researchers track a global virus
item.description: While the highly virulent avian influenza strain has only recently been discovered on Australian shores, researchers at Deakin University have been working behind the scenes for years, anticipating what an outbreak might look like. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists find breast cancer cells hiding behind protective “shields”
item.description: Researchers have mapped breast tumors in striking detail and uncovered hidden pockets of dormant cancer cells that may help explain why cancer can return after treatment. Unlike rapidly dividing cells, these quiet cells can essentially hibernate, allowing them to evade chemotherapy and reactivate later. The team found that they are often surrounded by immune cells and connective tissue cells that may act like a protective shield. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: This lifestyle program improved cognition 55% more than basic health advice
item.description: Older adults at risk of dementia improved their memory and thinking after following lifestyle programs combining exercise, healthy eating, cognitive training, and social engagement. Those who received regular coaching and structured support improved substantially more than participants given general health advice. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover a hidden problem with this popular sugar substitute
item.description: Sorbitol, a sugar alcohol commonly used in sugar-free candy, gum, and other low-calorie foods, may not be as harmless as it seems. Researchers at Washington University in St. Louis found that the body can convert sorbitol into a form of fructose in the liver, potentially triggering some of the same harmful metabolic effects linked to fructose. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: The extinct American 'cheetah' was not a cheetah after all
item.description: With their slender bodies and long front legs, Miracinonyx trumani—often nicknamed the "American cheetah"—was long thought to be a North American analog of the African big cat. But in a new study published in the journal Current Biology, researchers reveal that the extinct cat was more closely related to pumas. Some populations living near the Arctic preyed almost exclusively on fish, challenging the long-held assumption that these "cheetahs" chased fast-running prey, such as pronghorns. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: The Pantone color of the year for 2026 is white. It's called Cloud Dancer, which is described as a "lofty white." This choice reflects a growing trend away from color in our visual world. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Quiet' pulsar suddenly reveals three glitches in 15 years of observations
item.description: Using more than 15 years of observations from the Parkes radio telescope, astronomers detected three rotational glitches in the pulsar PSR J1637−4642—a young neutron star that had shown no signs of glitches since its discovery. The three glitches included one that changed its rotation rate by nearly 3 parts per million. Their paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Aug. 20. It has been accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal Letters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI can now control fusion plasma faster than humans can react
item.description: Princeton researchers have tested an AI system that can monitor and control fusion plasma in milliseconds, reacting far faster than a human operator. In one experiment, it predicted a damaging instability about 200 milliseconds before it appeared and adjusted the plasma to stop it from forming. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists find a weak spot in one of the deadliest brain cancers
item.description: Researchers may have found a new way to weaken glioblastoma’s defenses against treatment. Blocking a protein called SET prevented tumors from forming in preclinical models, while targeting related proteins made cancer cells more vulnerable to radiation. The strategy works by restoring activity of PP2A, an enzyme that glioblastoma cells appear to suppress. Human testing will be needed to determine whether the approach is safe and effective. Fuente: ScienceDaily.
